title: In each pair of angles, which one is greater and why?
description: One figure with the vertex O holds three pairs of angles. In the first two pairs one angle lies inside the other, and in the third pair the points B and C sit on the same ray from O. The checks use the same laying-over method as the book, and the video breaks the slip that a longer ray makes a bigger angle.
teaching_notes: One idea: when one angle lies inside another with the same vertex, the outer one is greater, and when the arms lie on the same rays the angles are equal. Watch for students who think a longer ray makes a bigger angle.

video_script.why: The child decides which angle is greater by seeing which lies inside the other, and when the arms lie on the same rays.
video_script.substitution: the book's own figure with the vertex O, the rays OA, OX and OY, and the points B and C on one ray
video_script.anchor: the figure of the book with the vertex O and the rays OA, OX, OY, OB and OC
video_script.payoff_line: Angle eigh oh bee is greater in the first two pairs, and the third pair is equal

final_answer.value: AOB is greater in the first pair; AOB is greater in the second pair; the third pair is equal
final_answer.spoken: angle eigh oh bee is greater in the first two pairs, and the third pair is equal

maths_rules: figure: O is the vertex; OA is upright; OX and OY slant, with OX steeper; B and C lie on the same horizontal ray, B nearer O
first pair: angle XOY lies inside angle AOB, so AOB is greater
second pair: angle XOB lies inside angle AOB, so AOB is greater
third pair: B and C lie on one ray from O, so angle XOB and angle XOC have the same arms and are equal
slip: a longer ray does not make a bigger angle
video_script.design: One idea: lay the smaller-looking angle inside the other with the vertex together, and see which lies inside. One figure with the vertex O stays on the board.
open_questions: The verdicts follow the worklist's reading of the figure; the book's figure could not be viewed.
